newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway ministry denies Aker claim over Storebrand.
newsitem.headline: Norway ministry denies Aker claim over Storebrand.

text.p: The Norwegian Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it had denied a complaint by Aker RGI ASA against a ruling that the shareholdings of four investors in insurer Storebrand ASA would be seen as one entity.

Norwegian industrial holding group Aker RGI appealed to the ministry earlier this month over a ruling by the Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission that the separate Storebrand shareholdings of billionaire Kjell Inge Roekke, his two companies Ivory Enterprises Corp and Ivory AS, as well as those of Aker RGI, of which Roekke is the main shareholder, amounted to one stake under Norwegian regulations.
Under Norwegian law any single shareholder or entity is not permitted to hold more than 10 percent in a financial institution. The four entities together hold more than 16 percent in Storebrand.

In a statement, the Finance Ministry said the group could not own more than 10 percent of the share capital in Storebrand. It added that the group could not vote for more than 10 percent of the votes in the company, or vote more than 20 percent of the votes represented in Storebrand's general assembly.
The ruling of the commission and the ministry effectively curbs the voting rights of Roekke and his associates at Storebrand's annual general meeting.
Norway's largest insurer is due to hold an extraordinary general meeting on Thursday to vote on a proposed merger with Norway's second largest bank, Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA.

Storebrand has been at odds with Roekke and Aker RGI since April when Aker RGI raised questioned whether the rules for redeeming preference capital in Storebrand complied with securities legislation. If Aker RGI's opinion prevailed, it could have created problems in the proposed merger.
